blocks.x: Tell more about Emmett, um, how he got, did he ever tell you how he got started on the cornet? Did he use cornet or trumpet?

Well, his daddy, his daddy was a bass player in the, in the shrine band. Here, you see, and that's where, and his mother played piano. And, uh, they used to sit around at home and play, and that's how he, he never did play, well, he played, he started with a guitar. And a banjo.

And then, and then that, they didn't like that so much. And even a little piano, according, and his mother played in, played real fine church piano, you know. And, uh, his sister played piano and sang, uh, spirituals. And he had an uncle who's quite well known as an author. His name is Kennedy, Emmett Kennedy. He's written a lot of books and things like that. And he was, he was a piano player, too. It's just natural in, in the family, you see. And, uh, then, once he hit the carnet, well, and he, and he never did play trumpet. He played carnet. They went to, he and, he and, uh, when he was with the Rhythm Kings, he and Paul Morez and Chink Martin went to this higher B.J. company. And, and, and they had a, uh, uh, he and Paul both had an instrument made called, uh, it was a, you could make it either a trumpet or a carnet. It had a, it had a, uh, the mouth pipe, you know. Yeah. And you could pull it out or shove it in. And you could make it either a trumpet or a carnet. And they had them custom, custom made, you know. It was something new and then nobody had seen anything like that. And, uh, but he, he, he never did like the, the, the trumpet sound. He always liked the, the cornet sound. And he always played the cornet. And, uh, and, uh.
